title: Detection of supported cohomology bounds by geometric costalks
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, $S\subseteq|X|$ a subset stable under specialization, $a\in\mathbf Z$, and $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ in the ordinary small etale category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point] with underlying point $x$, define
$$C_{\bar x}K=R\Gamma_{\{x_0\}}(X_{(\bar x)},K|_{X_{(\bar x)}}),$$
where $X_{(\bar x)}$ is the strict localization with closed point $x_0$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and supported cohomology is the right derived kernel of restriction to the complementary open [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]; restrictions $K|_{X_{(\bar x)}}$ and $u^*K$ are (exact) inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then the following are equivalent:
(1) $H^m(C_{\bar x}K)=0$ for every $x\in S$, every geometric $\bar x$ over $x$, and every $m\leq a$;
(2) $H^mR\Gamma_Z(V,u^*K)=0$ for every affine etale $u:V\to X$, every closed reduced subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ with $u(|Z|)\subseteq S$, and every $m\leq a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-closed-immersion].
With $u_!$ the exact left adjoint to etale restriction (the sheafified sum over lifts [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]) and $\Lambda_Z$ the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], there is a natural equality of groups
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)}(u_!i_*\Lambda_Z[-m],K)\cong H^mR\Gamma_Z(V,u^*K).$$
These assertions hold without excellence or constructibility.

source.place: XVII Definition 1.1.1 and 5.2, cosupport half of the Gabber construction: agent-formulated local-to-global support-bound input; full Gabber proof source WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with complement $j$, write $P_ZF=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$ and $i^!_0F=i^*P_ZF$. The supported-kernel adjunction gives $P_ZF=i_*i^!_0F$, exactness of $i_*$, and $i_*\dashv i^!_0$ on abelian sheaves. These assertions extend to constant $\Lambda$-module sheaves: all maps are natural in $F$, so commute with multiplication by each scalar; the Hom bijection restricts to linear maps because a map commutes with each scalar exactly when its transpose does. Exact coefficient forgetting detects exactness. Thus these are the same supported kernels in the module category, not a different coefficient theory.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, support adjunction in its proof; scalar-linear restriction of that adjunction

proof.text: The inverse image $i^*$ is exact and left adjoint to $i_*$. Therefore $i_*$ preserves injectives. Since $i_*$ is exact and left adjoint to $i^!_0$, the latter also preserves injectives. Consequently $P_Z=i_*i^!_0$ preserves injectives. On a bounded-below injective representative $I$ of $L$ put $P_Z^RL=P_ZI=i_*Ri^!L$. This specifies the derived sheaf of supported sections on $T$. All its cohomology sheaves are supported on $|Z|$, since the terms vanish on the complementary open.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; injective-model construction of derived supported sheaves

proof.text: The same representative gives $R\Gamma_Z(T,L)=R\Gamma(T,P_Z^RL)$: both are represented by $\Gamma(T,P_ZI)$, since $P_ZI$ is a bounded-below complex of injectives. If $W\subseteq |Z|$ is closed, it also gives $R\Gamma_W(T,P_Z^RL)=R\Gamma_W(T,L)$, since a section supported on $W$ already lies in $P_ZI$, so $\Gamma_W(T,P_ZI)=\Gamma_W(T,I)$ in every degree. These identities depend only on the closed subsets, not on nilpotents in their scheme structures, because the defining restriction kernel uses only the complementary open.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; the two composite-functor identities on injective complexes

proof.text: We will use the following elementary calculation from the injective representative, for either global sections or sections with a fixed closed support, or the sheaf functor $P_Z$. If $L\in D^{\geq q}$, take $J^r=0$ for $r<q$ in such a representative. For a left exact functor $F$, $FJ$ vanishes below $q$ and $H^q(FJ)=\ker(FJ^q\to FJ^{q+1})=F(\ker(J^q\to J^{q+1}))=F(\mathcal H^qL)$. Thus $RF(L)$ has the same lower bound and its bottom cohomology is the underived functor of the bottom cohomology. No spectral sequence, convergence, or dimension bound is needed.

source.place: Tags 05TI and 05TC, lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived and lemma-negative-vanishing; bottom-degree kernel calculation

proof.text: For an etale map $v:T'\to T$, restriction sends injective module sheaves to injectives. Sectionwise the kernels satisfy $(P_ZF)|_{T'}=P_{Z\times_TT'}(F|_{T'})$: on an etale object $B\to T'$ both are the kernel of $F(B)\to F(B\setminus (Z\times_T B))$. Applying this to an injective representative gives $v^*P_Z^RL=P_{Z\times_TT'}^R(v^*L)$ and the corresponding formulas for supported sections on etale objects. Exactness of inverse image identifies its cohomology sheaves with the inverse images of the cohomology sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, definition on etale objects; restriction of injective representatives

proof.text: All affine etale schemes used below are Noetherian. Indeed, etale maps are locally of finite presentation; their affine source has a finite cover by affine charts with finitely presented, hence finite-type, coordinate algebras over Noetherian affine charts of the base. Those algebras are Noetherian. For an affine Noetherian $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and a geometric point $\bar t$ over the prime $\mathfrak p$, the affine strict-local comparison identifies the ring of $T_{(\bar t)}$, as a $B$-algebra, with a strict henselization of $B_{\mathfrak p}$; $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian by localization, and its strict henselization by the strict-henselization theorem. For an affine scheme $T$, its strict-localization map $T_{(\bar t)}\to T$ is affine and ind-etale by the affine-chart strict-henselization lemma. These verify the hypotheses of the ind-etale supported base-change theorem whenever we use it.

source.place: Strict-localization prerequisites; Noetherian local rings and affine ind-etale strict localizations

proof.text: Here is the geometry at a generic point of a closed support. Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $E=V(J)$, and let $t=\mathfrak p$ be a generic point of an irreducible component of $E$, so $\mathfrak p$ is minimal among primes containing $J$. Let $C$ be the ring of $T_{(\bar t)}$. The affine strict-local comparison gives a $B$-algebra isomorphism of $C$ with a strict henselization of $B_{\mathfrak p}$, so every element of $B$ outside $\mathfrak p$, already a unit in $B_{\mathfrak p}$, is a unit in $C$; the chart maximal-ideal lemma (with the identity chart of $T$, whose ring map is the structural one) gives that the maximal ideal of $C$ is $\mathfrak p C$. A prime of $C$ lying over $E$ therefore contracts to a prime containing $J$ and contained in $\mathfrak p$; by minimality its contraction is $\mathfrak p$, so it contains $\mathfrak p C$ and is the maximal ideal. Hence the inverse image of $E$ in $T_{(\bar t)}$ is exactly its closed point. This argument applies also to $E=\overline{\{t\}}$ for any $t$.

source.place: Strict localization at the generic point of a support; the maximal-ideal formula in the strict-henselization construction

proof.text: For the strict-localization map $g:T'\to T$ of an affine Noetherian scheme and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$, ind-etale supported base change gives $h^*Ri^!L\cong Ri'^!g^*L$. The same theorem specifies the closed direct-image base-change isomorphism $g^*i_*\cong i'_*h^*$. Combining them gives $g^*P_Z^RL\cong P_{Z\times_TT'}^R(g^*L)$. For an etale $v:T\to X$, the strict-local invariance theorem identifies $T_{(\bar t)}$ with $X_{(v\bar t)}$ over $X$. Thus the closed-point supported cohomology after either strict localization is the costalk in the statement.

source.place: Tags 03Q9, 0A45 and 09XQ, ind-etale support base change and strict-local invariance

proof.text: Assume (1) and fix affine etale $u:V\to X$ and $Z$ as in (2). Put $L=u^*K$, $M=P_Z^RL$. Fix $b$ with $K\in D^{\geq b}$; Steps 4 and 5 give $M\in D^{\geq b}$. If some $\mathcal H^qM\ne0$ with $q\leq a$, choose the least such $q$ (among the integers at least $b$), so $M\in D^{\geq q}$. A nonzero sheaf has a nonzero section $s$ on some affine etale $W\to V$ (restrict any nonzero section to an affine cover). The zero-open lemma shows that its support $E\subset W$ is nonempty and closed and that its germ is nonzero at every point of $E$. Since $\mathcal H^qM$ is supported on $Z$, $E\subseteq Z\times_VW$. Choose an irreducible component of $E$ and its generic point $w$, using finite decomposition of closed subsets and sobriety. Then $u(w)\in S$.

source.place: Tags 04FR and 04FT, zero locus and closed support of a section; generic point of that closed support

proof.text: Choose a geometric $\bar w$ over $w$ and pull $M|_W$ and $s$ back to $T=W_{(\bar w)}$. Its pullback $N$ is in $D^{\geq q}$ by exactness. The pulled-back section of $\mathcal H^qN$ is supported at the closed point by Step 7: it is zero off the inverse image of $E$, since $s$ was already zero on $W\setminus E$. Its closed-point germ is nonzero by inverse-image compatibility with germs. Thus $\Gamma_{\{w_0\}}(T,\mathcal H^qN)\ne0$. Step 4 identifies this with $H^qR\Gamma_{\{w_0\}}(T,N)$. Steps 5 and 8 identify $N$ with $P_{Z_T}^R(K|_T)$, and $w_0\in Z_T$. Step 3 then identifies this nonzero group with $H^qR\Gamma_{\{w_0\}}(T,K|_T)=H^q(C_{u\bar w}K)$. This contradicts (1). Hence $M\in D^{\geq a+1}$.

source.place: Tags 04FR, 03Q9, 09XQ and 0A45; the generic-support section produces a nonzero bottom costalk

proof.text: By Step 3, $R\Gamma_Z(V,u^*K)=R\Gamma(V,M)$. Global sections is left exact, so the injective calculation in Step 4 applied to $M\in D^{\geq a+1}$ makes this complex concentrated in degrees at least $a+1$. This is precisely (2).

source.place: Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing; global sections of a complex with a lower cohomological bound

proof.text: Conversely assume (2). Let $V\to X$ be affine etale and let $Z\subseteq V$ be closed with image in $S$. Then $M=P_Z^R(K|_V)$ is in $D^{\geq a+1}$. To see this, otherwise choose its first nonzero $\mathcal H^qM$, $q\leq a$, as in Step 9, and a nonzero section on an affine etale $W\to V$. Steps 4 and 5 identify this section group with $H^qR\Gamma(W,M|_W)=H^qR\Gamma_{Z_W}(W,K|_W)$, the latter by Step 3. Replace $Z_W$ by the reduced induced closed subscheme: Step 3 shows that the complex is unchanged. The composite $W\to X$ is affine etale as an object of the small site (its source is affine), and the image of this reduced support is in $S$. Hypothesis (2) makes the displayed group zero, a contradiction. This proves the claimed sheaf bound for every such $Z$.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, bottom-degree detection by sections on affine etale objects; reduction does not change the complement

proof.text: Fix $x\in S$ and any geometric $\bar x$ over $x$. Choose an affine open $V\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and give $Z=\overline{\{x\}}\cap V$ its reduced induced structure. Specialization stability ensures $Z\subseteq S$. Step 12 gives $P_Z^R(K|_V)\in D^{\geq a+1}$. Pull this to $T=V_{(\bar x)}$, which the strict-local invariance theorem for the open (hence etale) immersion $V\hookrightarrow X$ identifies with $X_{(\bar x)}$ over $X$, closed point to closed point. By Step 7, the inverse image of $Z$ is the closed point; Step 8 identifies the pullback with $P_{\{x_0\}}^R(K|_T)$. Its lower bound is preserved by exact pullback. Taking derived global sections preserves that bound by Step 4. Step 3 identifies the result with $C_{\bar x}K$. Thus $H^mC_{\bar x}K=0$ for $m\leq a$, proving (1). The choice of $\bar x$ was arbitrary.

source.place: Tags 09XQ and 0A45; strict localization of the closure of a point and the supported base-change comparison

proof.text: Finally take a bounded-below injective representative $I$ of $K$. Exact etale extension and restriction form the adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$; in particular $u^*I$ is injective termwise. The localization-to-derived-Hom bijection computes $\operatorname{Hom}_D(u_!i_*\Lambda_Z[-m],K)$ by chain maps into $I$ modulo homotopy. Termwise adjunction identifies its Hom complex with $\operatorname{Hom}_V(i_*\Lambda_Z,u^*I)$. The scalar-linear supported adjunction of Step 1 identifies this complex with $\Gamma(Z,i^!_0u^*I)=\Gamma_Z(V,u^*I)$: a linear map from the rank-one constant module is determined by the image of $1$, and conversely any global section gives such a map. Taking $H^m$ proves the stated natural group isomorphism; the shift $[-m]$ places its source in degree $m$. All identifications are functorial (adjunctions, kernels and evaluation at $1$), so the isomorphism is natural in $K$. None of these steps uses excellence, constructibility, invertibility of a coefficient characteristic, or finite dimension.
